# XYZ Broker sandbox: API contract

Build against this document. The mock server's source is included so you can run it, but treat it
as you would a real backend you can't see into. This document is what we'll talk about.

**For the take-home** you need the conventions, `summary`, the submit endpoint, idempotency, the codes
and the sandbox test amounts. The cash outs list, live updates and the stream controls are for the
live call. You can skip them for now.

Base URL: `http://10.0.2.2:8080` from the Android emulator (`http://localhost:8080` on the host, or on
a device after `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080`). The sandbox serves cleartext HTTP; production is
HTTPS only.

Every request except `/_mock/reset` needs `Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]`.
A missing or wrong token is `401` with code `UNAUTHENTICATED`.

The one account in the sandbox is `100245`, in `USD`.

## Conventions

### Money

Amounts aren't typed the same way everywhere. The production service is the same.

| Where | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `GET …/summary`: `balance`, `equity`, `freeMargin` | JSON number, up to 4 decimals | `1250.5000` |
| `POST …/cashouts` request: `amount` | JSON number, at most 2 decimals, no exponent form | `250.00` |
| `POST …/cashouts` success: `amount` | decimal string, 2 decimals | `"250.00"` |
| Error bodies: `minimum`, `maxWithdrawable` | JSON number, 2 decimals | `1250.50` |
| `GET …/cashouts`: `amount` | decimal string, 2 decimals | `"250.00"` |

A request whose `amount` is a string, has more than two decimals, or uses exponent notation (`1.0E7`)
is refused with `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

### Dates

`createdAt` is ISO-8601 with an offset, either `Z` or `±hh:mm`, with or without fractional
seconds. Both forms appear in the same list:

```
2026-10-14T09:30:00Z
2026-10-02T11:15:42.123+01:00
```

`estimatedArrival` is a date only, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

### Errors

Errors come in three shapes, and the app needs to handle all of them.

**1. Problem body.** Any `4xx`/`5xx` the service itself produced:

```json
{ "code": "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "detail": "Amount is more than can be withdrawn.",
  "correlationId": "0f6c…", "maxWithdrawable": 1250.50 }
```

Branch on `code` only. `detail` is English text meant for our logs. It isn't written for customers, so
don't show it to them. `correlationId` is what support will ask for. Some codes carry extra fields
(see the table).

**2. Legacy refusal.** `200 OK` with `{ "isSuccess": false, "errorCode": "WITHDRAWAL_FAILED" }`.
Despite the 200, it's a refusal. Only the submit endpoint sends it.

**3. Gateway errors.** A `502`/`503`/`504` can come from the load balancer in front of the service,
with an HTML body and no `code`.

Separately, you may get no response at all (a timeout or a connection reset).

## Endpoints

### `GET /v1/accounts/{accountNumber}/summary`

```json
{ "accountNumber": "100245", "currency": "USD", "status": "active",
  "balance": 34412.6500, "equity": 36120.5512, "freeMargin": 34347.2000, "version": 1000 }
```

`version` is explained under "Live updates".

Available to cash out is the smallest of `balance`, `equity` and `freeMargin`, floored to the cent
(never rounded up). The service refuses anything above it.

### `POST /v1/accounts/{accountNumber}/cashouts`

Headers: `Idempotency-Key: <string>` (required, see below), `Content-Type: application/json`.

```json
{ "amount": 250.00,
  "method": "bank",
  "destination": { "beneficiaryName": "A. Customer", "iban": "GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32" },
  "reason": "Rent" }
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `amount` | number, at most 2 decimals. Minimum **50.00** |
| `method` | must be `"bank"` |
| `beneficiaryName` | 2–70 characters after trimming (counted in UTF-16 code units, so an emoji can count as 2) |
| `iban` | spaces and case are ignored. Length by country and the mod-97 check are enforced for `GB DE FR IE ES NL BE IT` only; any other country is `INVALID_IBAN` |
| `reason` | optional, up to 140 characters (counted the same way) |

Every invalid field is reported at once in `fieldErrors` (on a `422`), keyed by field name, with one of
these values: `amount`: `INVALID_AMOUNT`; `method`: `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`; `beneficiaryName`:
`INVALID_NAME`; `iban`: `INVALID_IBAN`; `reason`: `TOO_LONG`. A body that is not a JSON object is
`400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with no `fieldErrors`.

Success, `200`:

```json
{ "isSuccess": true, "cashoutId": "5b0c…", "reference": "CO-5A1D0C21", "status": "processing",
  "amount": "250.00", "currency": "USD", "estimatedArrival": "2026-10-23" }
```

The account is debited immediately, but nothing is paid until a person approves it. That's why the
status is `processing`.

### `GET /v1/accounts/{accountNumber}/cashouts`

Newest first.

```json
{ "items": [
  { "id": "4444…", "reference": "CO-9D2E6B13", "amount": "500.00", "currency": "USD",
    "status": "approved", "createdAt": "2026-10-15T08:00:00+00:00",
    "destinationLabel": "IBAN ••••1332", "cancellable": false } ],
  "version": 1000 }
```

`status` is currently one of `processing`, `completed`, `rejected` or `cancelled`, but more values are
coming (the sandbox list already has one that isn't among those four). Treat a status you don't
recognise as still in progress, and never show it as completed. `cancellable` is for a future
feature; you can ignore it.

### `GET /v1/accounts/{accountNumber}/stream`

Live updates for the account, as [server-sent events](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html)
(`text/event-stream`). Same `Authorization` header as everything else. See "Live updates" below.

### `POST /_mock/reset`

Sandbox only, no auth. Restores the starting state, forgets every idempotency key and closes any open
streams.

## Live updates

The stream carries three event types. Every `data` line is a JSON object.

| `event` | `data` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `account` | `balance`, `equity`, `freeMargin` (numbers, up to 4 decimals, as in `summary`), `version` | whenever any of them changes. Equity moves with the market, many times a second |
| `cashout` | a full list item (as in `GET …/cashouts`), plus `version` | a cash out is created or its status or `cancellable` changes |
| `heartbeat` | `version`, `serverTime` | every 5 seconds, whatever else is happening |

How `version` works:

- It's one counter for the whole account. Every change to the account or its cash outs takes the next
  number, so on a healthy connection consecutive `account` and `cashout` events go up by exactly 1.
  A heartbeat repeats the latest version; it doesn't take a new one.
- `summary` and the cash outs list both include the `version` they reflect.
- The stream doesn't send the current state when you connect. Get that from `summary` and the list,
  and use `version` to line the two up.
- If the numbers jump, you've missed something. The stream can't re-send it, so re-read `summary` and
  the list.
- Events are usually in order, but not always. One with a `version` you've already passed is out of
  date.
- If nothing at all arrives (not even a heartbeat), the connection may be open but not delivering.

The stream does not resume where it left off after a disconnect. In the sandbox, `equity` moves on its
own while a stream is open, but `freeMargin` only changes when money moves or you use
`/_mock/market-move` (below), so the available figure stays predictable. A new cash out goes from
`processing` to `approved` after 30 seconds (`PROGRESS_MS`) and to `completed` 30 seconds after that.

## Idempotency

The submit endpoint moves money, so it is designed to be safe to repeat.

- `Idempotency-Key` is required. Missing: `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`.
- The first time a key is seen with a request that passes field validation, the service decides the
  outcome and stores it for 24 hours. That includes refusals such as `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`.
  `429` responses are not stored. `VALIDATION_ERROR` is checked before the key is looked at and is
  never stored.
- The same key with the same body gets the stored outcome again, with the response header
  `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. It never debits twice.
- The same key with a different body is `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
- The stored outcome is what the service *decided*, even when the response to that first attempt was
  lost, late or replaced by a gateway error.
- A different key is a different request. It debits again.

## Codes

| HTTP | `code` | Meaning | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` | no `Idempotency-Key` | |
| 400 / 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | body not valid JSON, or fields invalid | `fieldErrors`: map of field to reason, e.g. `{"iban":"INVALID_IBAN"}` |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | bad token | |
| 403 | `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` | account may not move money. Nothing debited | |
| 404 | `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` | unknown account | |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | no such route | |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | the sandbox itself failed unexpectedly. On a submit, the outcome is unknown | |
| 409 | `WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT` | the outcome could not be determined and needs a human. **Money may or may not have moved** | `supportReference` |
| 422 | `BELOW_MINIMUM` | under the minimum. Nothing debited | `minimum` |
| 422 | `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | above available. Nothing debited | `maxWithdrawable` |
| 422 | `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` | see above | |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | too many requests. Nothing debited. Also sent as a `Retry-After` header | `retryAfterSeconds` |
| 200 | (`errorCode` `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED`) | legacy refusal. Nothing debited | |

## Sandbox test amounts

The sandbox misbehaves on purpose for these exact amounts (all valid, all under available) so that
you can see the failure paths without waiting for production to produce them. Every other amount
that passes validation succeeds.

| Amount | What happens |
|---|---|
| `200.00` | `403 ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` |
| `300.00` | The cashout **is processed and the account debited**, but the response is held back for 15 seconds (`STALL_MS`), long enough for most HTTP clients to give up |
| `400.00` | `200` with `isSuccess: false`, `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED` |
| `500.00` | The cashout **is processed and the account debited**, but the first response is a `502` HTML page |
| `600.00` | `429 RATE_LIMITED`, `retryAfterSeconds: 30` |
| `700.00` | `409 WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT` with a `supportReference` |

Reset between experiments with `POST /_mock/reset`.

## Sandbox stream controls

These make the stream misbehave on demand. All are `POST`, need no auth, and return `204`.

| Path | What happens |
|---|---|
| `/_mock/stream/drop` | Every open stream is cut off |
| `/_mock/stream/stall` | Streams stay open but nothing is sent, heartbeats included, for 20 seconds (`STREAM_STALL_MS`). Changes made during that time are not re-sent |
| `/_mock/stream/gap` | The newest `processing` cash out becomes `approved`, and the event for that change is never sent (`409` with code `NOTHING_TO_CHANGE` if there isn't one) |
| `/_mock/stream/replay` | An out-of-date `cashout` event arrives late: its `version` is lower than events the stream has already sent |
| `/_mock/market-move` | A market move against the account: `equity` and `freeMargin` both fall by 1,000.00, so the available figure does too |

With `LOG=1` the sandbox prints how many streams are open each time one opens or closes.

# Android exercise: Cash out

Thanks for getting this far. This is the take-home part of the process. It's one small screen, and
we expect you to use AI tools while you build it, the same way we do day to day.

**Time:** aim for about 75 minutes and please stop at 90. A smaller submission with good judgement in
it beats a bigger one. If you run out of time, write down what you'd have done next.

## The scenario

XYZ Broker is a trading app. Customers hold a margin account and can ask to take money out to their
bank. You're building the Android "Cash out" screen against our sandbox service.

A cash out is a request. The account is debited straight away, and someone on our payments team
approves the payout later. So a successful submit means the request was received and is being
processed. The money hasn't been paid yet.

## What to build

A native Android app in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose, minSdk 26. Our iOS app is SwiftUI, so Compose is
what we'd use on Android too. One screen:

```
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  Cash out                    │
│                              │
│  Available   $12,480.00      │
│                              │
│  Amount      [ 250.00     ]  │
│  Min $50.00                  │
│                              │
│  Beneficiary name [        ] │
│  IBAN             [        ] │
│                              │
│  [        Cash out        ]  │
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

(Rough layout only. The figures are made up.)

- Show how much the customer can take out. The rule for working this out is in `API.md` under
  "summary".
- Take an amount, the beneficiary name and an IBAN.
- If the amount is certain to be refused, stop the customer before they send it and tell them why in
  plain language. You don't need to check the IBAN on the device: the service does, and its
  `fieldErrors` should show against the right field.
- Submit to the service and show the outcome for every way a submit can end, including the cases
  where the app can't be sure what happened. `API.md` lists them, and the sandbox will produce each
  one on demand (see "Sandbox test amounts"). Outcomes that mean the same thing to a customer can
  share a message.
- On success, tell the customer the request is processing and show its reference and estimated
  arrival date.

## Rules

1. **Money.** The app must never display, compute or send an amount that's off by even one cent.
2. **The app writes its own customer-facing messages.** Don't show messages written by the server
   (like `detail`) to the customer. Decide what each situation should say and word it yourself. Data
   such as references and dates is fine to show.
3. **Never debit a customer twice for one intention.** If anything the app does could cause that,
   treat it as a bug.
4. **Be honest about what the app knows.** If it can't tell whether the money has moved, it shouldn't
   say that it has, or that it hasn't.
5. `API.md` describes how the sandbox behaves. If you find somewhere it doesn't, mention it in your
   notes. We'd like to know.

## Out of scope

Login (use the token in `API.md`), the cash outs list, live updates, the optional `reason` field,
crypto, other payout methods, localisation beyond English, offline support, and visual polish beyond
clear and usable. Feel free to mention anything you'd add.

## Running the sandbox

```
cd mock-server
node server.mjs          # Node 18 or later, nothing to install
```

It listens on port 8080. From the emulator, use `http://10.0.2.2:8080`. `POST /_mock/reset` puts it
back to its starting state. You can set `STALL_MS` or `LATENCY_MS` in the environment to change its
delays, and `LOG=1` makes it print every request it gets, which is handy for checking what your app
actually sent.

## AI use

Use whatever tools you like: chat assistants, IDE agents, code generation. What we're looking at is
your engineering judgement while you use them: what you ask for, what you check, what you throw
away, and whether you can stand behind what you ship.

Please include:

- **Your AI conversation history.** Export it, share links or commit the session logs, whatever your
  tool supports. We do read them. Messy is fine. Please don't tidy them up afterwards. If you wrote
  something by hand, just say so.
- **The tools and models you used.**

Using AI heavily won't count against you. Shipping code you didn't check, or not being able to
explain your own submission, will.

## What to submit

A private Git repository (or a zip) with:

1. The Android project. It should build with `./gradlew assembleDebug` from a clean checkout.
2. Tests that you've run, covering at least how you work out the available figure and what your app
   sends when a submit is retried.
3. A short `NOTES.md` (half a page is plenty):
   - assumptions you made where the brief or `API.md` was silent or ambiguous
   - the decision you're least sure of, and why
   - what you'd do with another hour
4. The AI logs and tool list described above.

## What happens next

If it goes well, we'll set up a 60-minute call. You'll share your screen, take us through your code
and add a small feature to it live with whatever tools you normally use. There's nothing to prepare
beyond knowing your own submission. We'll send you an updated sandbox at the start of the call.

If you have questions while you're working, reply to the email this came with and ask the way you'd
ask a colleague. Asking (or not) won't count against you.

Good luck, and thanks for your time.

# Architecture

One Android `app` module, with four architecture packages under `com.xyzbroker.cashoutapp`. Package names use lowercase Kotlin conventions, including `di`.

```text
app/src/main/java/com/xyzbroker/cashoutapp/
├── CashOutApplication.kt
├── MainActivity.kt
├── di/
├── data/
│   ├── remote/
│   │   ├── api/
│   │   ├── dto/
│   │   └── network/
│   │       └── common/
│   ├── mapper/
│   └── repository/
├── domain/
│   ├── model/
│   ├── result_handlimg/
│   ├── repository/
│   └── usecase/
└── presentation/
    ├── theme/
    └── cashout/
        └── components/
```

Each scaffold package contains a README describing its responsibility and planned files. Theme Kotlin files have been moved into presentation/theme, with their packages and activity import updated. No placeholder Kotlin implementations have been added.

## Dependencies

Presentation → Domain ← Data. DI wires implementations to interfaces. Domain does not import Android, Retrofit, DTOs, or presentation types. These boundaries are conventions within the single module, not Gradle-enforced module boundaries.

## Presentation contract

CashOutViewModel.kt will contain both the ViewModel and CashOutUiState definition. The ViewModel owns MutableStateFlow internally and exposes read-only StateFlow. CashOutRoute collects it with lifecycle awareness and passes state and event callbacks into stateless CashOutScreen and component composables.

Expected states: initial loading, editable form, submitting, request received, and error. Submission success must not imply payment completion. Prevent repeated submit taps while a request is in progress. Follow the sandbox API contract for idempotency, retry behavior, balance refresh, and validation.

## Planned classes

- DI: NetworkModule, RepositoryModule.
- Data: CashOutApi, NetworkClient, request/response DTOs, CashOutMapper, CashOutRepositoryImpl.
- Domain: AccountBalance, Money, CashOutRequest, CashOutRepository, GetCashOutDetailsUseCase, ValidateCashOutAmountUseCase, SubmitCashOutUseCase.
- Presentation: CashOutRoute, CashOutScreen, CashOutViewModel (including CashOutUiState), AmountInput, CashOutConfirmation.

These classes are planned until their implementation is explicitly recorded in the change log.

## Dependency injection setup

Hilt and its KSP compiler are configured. CashOutApplication initializes Hilt and MainActivity is an Android entry point. NetworkModule provides Retrofit, OkHttp, authorization headers, and debug logging with Authorization redaction. Repository bindings remain planned.

## Domain errors

CashOutError.kt defines endpoint-specific reasons in domain/result_handlimg. NetworkHandler.kt defines the sealed result hierarchy in data/remote/network/common and is independent of endpoint-specific domain reasons. Domain remains independent of data. See [error handling](ERROR_HANDLING.md) for all supplied codes, extra fields, and ambiguous submit outcomes. Error parsing and mapping in data remain pending.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. I've read the brief and checked where the repo stands. You didn't say what you want next, so here's what I found and a proposed plan.

## Things to fix first

**1. The bearer token is hardcoded.** `di/NetworkModule.kt:40` has the sandbox token ([REDACTED]) written directly in the source, and it's already committed. Your brief also contains the same value.
- It's a candidate sandbox token, so the risk is low. Our policy still treats any pasted or committed credential as exposed. Ask the reviewers whether it should be rotated.
- Fix: read it from `local.properties` (gitignored) or an environment variable into a `BuildConfig` field. Commit a `local.properties.example` (or `.env.example`) that has a placeholder value.

**2. Cleartext HTTP.** The sandbox only serves `http://`. Allow cleartext for `10.0.2.2` and `localhost` only, using a debug or uat `network_security_config`. Don't turn it on for the whole app, and keep prod HTTPS-only.

**3. Docs out of date.** `docs/CHANGELOG.md` says minSdk 24, but `AppConfig.MIN_SDK` is already 26, which is what the brief requires. I'll fix the docs when I next touch them.

**4. Stack note.** Our org default stack is Python. This assignment requires Kotlin and Compose, so I'll follow the brief.

## Design points the brief is testing
- **Money:** use `BigDecimal` from end to end. Parse `summary` numbers as `BigDecimal`, never `Double`. Available = `min(balance, equity, freeMargin)` rounded down to 2 decimals. Send `amount` as a JSON number with exactly 2 decimals and no exponent (Gson plus `toPlainString()`, tested).
- **Idempotency:** create one key per intention, meaning the amount, name and IBAN as entered. Reuse it on every retry of that same request. Make a new key only when the user edits the form or a request has a final outcome. You need a test that shows a retry sends the same key and the same body.
- **Outcomes that are certain:** success, `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED`, `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED`, `BELOW_MINIMUM`, `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, `RATE_LIMITED` (wait for `Retry-After`) and the 422 `fieldErrors` shown on each field.
- **Outcomes that are unknown:** timeout, connection reset, 502/503/504 HTML pages, `INTERNAL_ERROR` and `WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT`. Never say these failed. Offer "Check again", which retries with the **same** key and gets the stored result back.
- **Timeout:** the read timeout is currently 30s, so the `300.00` stall (15s) will just succeed. A shorter timeout would exercise the unknown-outcome path. Either way, it's worth a line in NOTES.md.

1. Move the token into config and add the cleartext config.
2. Domain: `Money` helpers, the available-figure calculation, amount validation, and the outcome model.
3. Data: DTOs, API, error parsing for all three error shapes, and the repository.
4. The ViewModel with state and idempotency key handling, plus stateless screens.
5. Unit tests for the available figure, amount serialization, and retries reusing the same key and body.
6. NOTES.md, docs and CHANGELOG.

# Error handling

Endpoint-specific CashOutError reasons live in domain/result_handlimg/CashOutError.kt. Generic NetworkHandler<T> lives in data/remote/network/common/NetworkHandler.kt and has Success(data), HttpError, ConnectionError, and UnexpectedError cases. It is a result type, not an Exception: success is returned, not thrown. HttpError preserves status, raw errorCode, optional message, and cause without depending on CashOutError. DTO parsing and domain mapping remain pending.

| HTTP | Code | Domain reason / extra fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED | IdempotencyKeyRequired |
| 400 / 422 | VALIDATION_ERROR | ValidationError(fieldErrors) |
| 401 | UNAUTHENTICATED | Unauthenticated |
| 403 | ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED | AccountRestricted |
| 404 | ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND | AccountNotFound |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | NotFound |
| 500 | INTERNAL_ERROR | InternalError; submit outcome unknown |
| 409 | WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT | WithdrawalNeedsSupport(supportReference); human support required |
| 422 | BELOW_MINIMUM | BelowMinimum(minimum) |
| 422 | INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS | InsufficientFunds(maxWithdrawable) |
| 422 | IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED | IdempotencyKeyReused |
| 429 | RATE_LIMITED | RateLimited(retryAfterSeconds) |
| Any non-success | Missing/unrecognized code | Unknown(rawCode) |
| 200 | errorCode=WITHDRAWAL_FAILED | CashOutError.WithdrawalFailed; legacy refusal |

Extra monetary values use BigDecimal to preserve precision; no currency or units are inferred. Optional extra fields are nullable so an incomplete error body does not erase the original failure. Field errors default to an empty map.

## Mapping contract for the upcoming data implementation

- Parse status and business code independently. Preserve unknown codes and HTTP status.
- An HTTP 200 body is transported as NetworkHandler.Success. Endpoint-specific mapping must inspect errorCode and map WITHDRAWAL_FAILED to CashOutError.WithdrawalFailed; transport success does not imply business success.
- For RATE_LIMITED, consume retryAfterSeconds and the Retry-After header according to the API contract; a header parser is not implemented yet.
- Map network I/O failures to ConnectionError. Preserve coroutine cancellation by rethrowing CancellationException rather than wrapping it.
- Use UnexpectedError for other unexpected failures. A malformed non-success body should retain HttpError with Unknown, rather than lose its HTTP status.
- INTERNAL_ERROR on submit, lost connections, and timeouts do not prove that nothing was debited. WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT explicitly requires human intervention; money may or may not have moved. Do not automatically retry these as a new request/key.
- ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED, BELOW_MINIMUM, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, RATE_LIMITED, and legacy WITHDRAWAL_FAILED explicitly mean nothing was debited per the supplied contract. Do not infer debit outcome for other codes without more contract details.

Not fully. It has a slot for every transport outcome, but it drops information that the domain needs for certain cases. For a submit, some of those losses decide whether the app can honestly say "nothing was debited". I checked every way the submit endpoint can end, as listed in `API.md`:

| How the submit ends | Where it lands today | Covered? |
|---|---|---|
| `200` with `isSuccess: true` | `Success(dto)` | ✅ |
| `200` with `isSuccess: false`, `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED` | `Success(dto)`, then the mapper checks `errorCode` | ✅, provided the DTO has nullable `isSuccess`/`errorCode` |
| `4xx`/`5xx` problem body | `HttpError(status, errorCode)` | ⚠️ the extra fields are dropped |
| `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` + `fieldErrors` | `HttpError` | ❌ no `fieldErrors`, so errors can't be shown on the right field |
| `422 BELOW_MINIMUM` / `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | `HttpError` | ❌ `minimum` / `maxWithdrawable` are lost |
| `409 WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT` | `HttpError` | ❌ `supportReference` is lost, and it's the one thing the customer needs |
| `429 RATE_LIMITED` | `HttpError` | ❌ the `retryAfterSeconds` field and the `Retry-After` header are both lost |
| Any problem body | — | ❌ `correlationId` is lost (support asks for it) |
| `502/503/504` HTML from the gateway | `HttpError(status, null)` if the HTML doesn't crash parsing | ⚠️ can't be told apart from "the service sent a body without a code" |
| Read timeout or connection reset after sending | `ConnectionError` | ⚠️ see point 1 |
| Can't connect at all (no network, refused, DNS) | `ConnectionError` | ⚠️ treated the same as a timeout |
| `200` whose body can't be parsed or is missing fields | probably `UnexpectedError` | ❌ on a submit this may have debited, but nothing says so |
| Coroutine cancelled while the request is in flight | not modelled | ⚠️ the request may already have reached the server |
| `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header | dropped | minor: only useful in logs |

## The real problems

**1. It doesn't say whether the request may have reached the server.** That's the key question for Rules 3 and 4, and only the transport layer can answer it.
- **Can't connect** (`ConnectException`, `UnknownHostException`): the request never went out, so nothing was debited.
- **Sent but no reply** (`SocketTimeoutException` on read, a reset partway through the response): the outcome is unknown.

`ConnectionError` merges the two. You have two honest options:
- **Split them**, so "check your connection" is only shown when you know nothing was sent.
- **Treat every connection error on submit as unknown.** This is simpler and still honest, and retrying with the same key is always safe. I'd do this for the take-home and say so in NOTES.md.

**2. `UnexpectedError` is ambiguous.** A `200` that fails to parse means "the server probably accepted it", not "something broke". On a submit, any response we can't interpret has to be treated as an unknown outcome, never as a refusal.

**3. `HttpError` keeps the code but drops the body and the headers.** By the time the domain sees it, the data it needs to build `CashOutError` is gone.

## Suggested shape

```kotlin
sealed interface NetworkResult<out T> {
    data class Success<T>(val data: T, val replayed: Boolean) : NetworkResult<T>

    /** The server answered with a non-2xx status. problem == null means no parseable body (e.g. gateway HTML). */
    data class HttpError(
        val status: Int,
        val problem: ProblemDto?,
        val retryAfterHeader: Long?,
    ) : NetworkResult<Nothing>

    /** The request may have reached the server: read timeout, reset, or an unparseable 2xx body. */
    data class NoUsableResponse(val cause: Throwable) : NetworkResult<Nothing>

    /** The request was never sent (connect failed). Optional if you treat all I/O as unknown. */
    data class NotSent(val cause: IOException) : NetworkResult<Nothing>
}

// data layer DTO: all nullable, money as BigDecimal
data class ProblemDto(
    val code: String?, val detail: String?, val correlationId: String?,
    val fieldErrors: Map<String, String>?, val minimum: BigDecimal?,
    val maxWithdrawable: BigDecimal?, val supportReference: String?,
    val retryAfterSeconds: Long?,
)
```

## How the domain decides

The mapper, not `NetworkResult`, turns each of these into `Accepted` / `Refused` / `Unknown`:
- `HttpError` where `problem == null` and the status is 502/503/504: **Unknown**.
- `HttpError` with `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT`, or an unrecognized code: **Unknown**.
- `HttpError` with `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED`, `BELOW_MINIMUM`, `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, `RATE_LIMITED` or `VALIDATION_ERROR`, plus a `Success` carrying `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED`: **Refused** (nothing debited).
- `NoUsableResponse`: **Unknown**.
- `NotSent`: Refused with a connection reason, or Unknown if you take the simpler route.

## Two smaller points
- **Cancellation:** rethrow `CancellationException`, as `ERROR_HANDLING.md` already says. Also run the submit in `viewModelScope` and keep the idempotency key in the ViewModel, so an interrupted submit can be retried with the same key and isn't lost.
- **Reading the error body:** `errorBody()` can only be read once. Read it as a string, try to parse it as JSON, and fall back to `problem = null` so HTML can't throw.

No. `CashOutError` stays in **domain**. Only the server's raw response format lives in data. There are three layers of types, and each layer owns its own:

| Type | Layer | What it knows about |
|---|---|---|
| `ProblemDto`, `CashOutResponseDto` | `data/remote/dto` | The JSON format: field names, nullable everything |
| `NetworkResult<T>` | `data/remote/network/common` | HTTP: status codes, headers, I/O failures |
| `CashOutError`, `SubmitOutcome` | `domain` | What happened, in business terms. No HTTP, no JSON |

The **mapper in data** is the only place where these meet. It turns HTTP into business terms:

```
API ──► NetworkResult<CashOutResponseDto> ──► CashOutMapper ──► SubmitOutcome (domain)
        (data)                                (data)            uses CashOutError (domain)
```

```kotlin
// domain/repository/CashOutRepository.kt  — no HTTP types here
interface CashOutRepository {
    suspend fun submit(request: CashOutRequest, idempotencyKey: String): SubmitOutcome
}

// data/mapper/CashOutMapper.kt  — data may import domain, never the reverse
fun NetworkResult<CashOutResponseDto>.toSubmitOutcome(): SubmitOutcome = when (this) {
    is NetworkResult.Success -> data.toOutcome()   // checks isSuccess / WITHDRAWAL_FAILED
    is NetworkResult.HttpError -> when (problem?.code) {
        "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS" -> Refused(CashOutError.InsufficientFunds(problem.maxWithdrawable))
        "WITHDRAWAL_NEEDS_SUPPORT" -> Unknown(problem.supportReference)
        null -> Unknown(null)                       // gateway HTML: outcome unknown
        // ...
        else -> Unknown(null)                       // unrecognized code on a submit
    }
    is NetworkResult.NoUsableResponse -> Unknown(null)
    is NetworkResult.NotSent -> Unknown(null)        // or Refused(connection), if you split them
}
```

So `CashOutError` is already in the right package (`domain/result_handlimg`). What changes is how it gets filled:
- Today `HttpError` only carries `errorCode`, so the mapper has no `maxWithdrawable`, `supportReference`, `fieldErrors` or the like to put into `CashOutError`.
- With `ProblemDto` carried inside `HttpError`, it does.

Two small optional changes to `CashOutError`:
1. **Drop the `code: String?` property from the base class.** It puts wire strings into domain. The mapper is the only place that needs the string-to-type mapping.
2. **Some members are never a refusal.** `InternalError`, `WithdrawalNeedsSupport` and `Unknown` don't mean "refused" on a submit. They belong under `SubmitOutcome.Unknown`, not `Refused`. You can keep them in `CashOutError` and let `SubmitOutcome` decide, or move them out. The first is less churn.

import com.xyzbroker.cashoutapp.data.remote.dto.ProblemDto
import java.io.IOException

/** Transport outcome of one HTTP call. Business meaning is decided by the endpoint mapper. */
sealed interface NetworkResult<out T> {

    /** 2xx with a parsed body. The body may still be a business refusal (e.g. WITHDRAWAL_FAILED). */
    data class Success<T>(
        val data: T,
        val replayed: Boolean,
    ) : NetworkResult<T>

    /** Non-2xx. problem is null when the body is not a problem JSON (e.g. gateway HTML). */
    data class HttpError(
        val status: Int,
        val problem: ProblemDto?,
        val retryAfterSeconds: Long?,
    ) : NetworkResult<Nothing>

    /** The request may have reached the server but no usable response came back. */
    data class NoUsableResponse(val cause: Throwable) : NetworkResult<Nothing>

    /** The request was never sent (connection could not be established). */
    data class NotSent(val cause: IOException) : NetworkResult<Nothing>
}

`NetworkHandler.kt` is replaced by `NetworkResult.kt`, plus `ProblemDto.kt` and a `safeApiCall` helper that sorts each call into one of the four results. All 11 new unit tests pass, and the prod variant compiles. I haven't built a minified release, so the new R8 keep rule is untested.

## Code
- **`NetworkResult.kt`:** the four cases we agreed: `Success(data, replayed)`, `HttpError(status, problem, retryAfterSeconds)`, `NoUsableResponse(cause)` and `NotSent(cause)`. The default English messages are gone.
- **`ProblemDto.kt`:** the error body, with every field nullable and money as `BigDecimal`.
- **`SafeApiCall.kt`:** the classification:
  - `NotSent` only when the connection itself failed and OkHttp hadn't already tried once. If OkHttp retried, the first attempt may have reached the server, so that case is `NoUsableResponse`.
  - Read timeouts, resets, empty or unparseable 2xx bodies, and any other unexpected exception all count as `NoUsableResponse`, because the server may have acted on the submit.
  - Error bodies are read once. HTML (e.g. a 502 from the gateway) gives `problem = null` instead of crashing.
  - It reads the `Retry-After` header (seconds form only) and the `Idempotent-Replayed` header.
  - `CancellationException` is rethrown.
- **`rules.keep`:** a keep rule for the `dto` package. Release builds are minified and Gson maps DTOs by reflection, so without it the fields would be stripped and parse as null.

## Tests
`SafeApiCallTest` has 11 tests. They use plain Retrofit `Response` objects, so no new dependencies were needed. They cover:
- the replay header;
- exact `BigDecimal` values (`1250.50`);
- `fieldErrors` and `Retry-After`;
- gateway HTML;
- `NotSent` vs `NoUsableResponse`, including after an OkHttp retry;
- an unparseable success body;
- cancellation.

## Docs
I updated `ERROR_HANDLING.md` (new table and rules for the upcoming mapper), `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`, the three package READMEs, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

Nothing is committed.

## Still open
- The token is still hardcoded in `NetworkModule.kt` ([REDACTED]), and `usesCleartextTraffic` is still on for the whole app, prod included.
- `BUILD_CONFIGURATION.md` and the CHANGELOG still say minSdk 24; the actual value is 26.
- The next step is the mapper from `NetworkResult` to `SubmitOutcome`, plus the API interface and the response DTOs.
